items.snippet: 《纽约时报》DealBook调查显示，企业CEO普遍认为AI推广顺利，但普通员工却持相反看法。
items.raw_snippet:
## DealBook

Surveys show workers and executives have different views on A.I.

When it comes to artificial intelligence, chief executives and their work forces aren’t seeing eye to eye.

Corporate leaders, increasingly in earnings calls and interviews, tout productivity gains and say they are doing right by their workers as they roll out the technology.

But workers are much more concerned about being supplanted, and they don’t trust their company’s executives. [...] A survey from the Milken Institute-Harris Poll Listening Project recently found that more than two-thirds of business leaders expect they will be better off financially in five years because of A.I., while just 27 percent of the U.S. work force felt the same way — a whopping 41 point gap. [...] Workers also see less A.I. transformation than leadership does. Nearly three-fourths of leaders say A.I. has significantly changed the way work is done, compared with 58 percent of entry and midlevel employees, according to a report released this month from the Wharton School.

items.snippet: Man in a suit operates a huge, early computer with multiple racks of visible wir...
items.raw_snippet:
Man in a suit operates a huge, early computer with multiple racks of visible wiring and components. Grayscale photo.:format(avif))

Generic AI acts like a new entry-level hire, permanently stuck at day one. The same can be said for AI that's been added to your existing tools, but not into your actual workflows. [...] 1. Could a new hire and an AI agent learn your firm the same way?   
   If a new manager asked how your firm runs a monthly close or reviews a return, is there something you'd hand them, or does the answer live in a few senior people's heads? AI can only be taught what has been written down or built into workflow templates.
2. Do your AI tools know your clients, or just the world? [...] You've spent years building how your firm works. But the firms that scale past the founder's calendar are the ones that turn expertise into an asset, not a bottleneck. Context is that asset: the manual that finally captures and puts that knowledge to work at a scale that wasn’t possible before AI.
